prompt_text: I need braces or Invisalign in Houston. Which specific orthodontists should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best orthodontist in Houston for braces or Invisalign?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I’ll find specific orthodontists near you and explain why each is a good call. To give accurate, local recommendations I need one quick detail:

- What ZIP code or neighborhood in Houston are you in (or willing to travel to)?
- Also: are you an adult or is this for a teen/child? Any insurance or price range limits? Do you already prefer Invisalign vs braces or are you open to both?

If you want a fast checklist now (so you can call places yourself), here are the exact criteria and call questions that will quickly tell you which offices to prioritize — and why those things matter:

What to look for (why it matters)
- Board-certified orthodontist (American Board of Orthodontics diplomate): shows extra testing and proven clinical competence.
- Specialist (orthodontist) rather than a general dentist offering Invisalign: specialists have 2–3 years extra training focused only on tooth movement.
- Invisalign provider level (Gold/Platinum/Preferred/Elite/Diamond): higher tiers mean the doctor does many Invisalign cases — useful for predictable aligner outcomes.
- Digital scanner (iTero/3Shape) and digital treatment simulation: faster, more comfortable records and better visualization of expected results.
- Before-and-after photos of cases similar to yours: shows relevant experience (e.g., crowding, gaps, bite correction).
- Clear pricing, financing, and insurance handling: avoids surprises; ask about total cost, monthly plans, and what’s included (retainers, emergency visits).
- Retention plan and follow-up frequency: good outcomes depend on retainers and proper follow-up.
- Hospital privileges/CBCT (if you have complex bite or jaw issues): indicates ability to handle more complex skeletal cases or coordinate surgical care.

Questions to ask on the phone (and what to expect)
- “Is Dr. X an orthodontic specialist and are they board-certified?” — Expect a clear yes/no; if yes they should say “ABO diplomate” if applicable.
- “How many Invisalign cases does Dr. X do per year, and do you have Gold/Platinum/Diamond status?” — Higher numbers/status indicate experience.
- “Do you use an intraoral scanner for impressions?” — Yes is better.
- “What’s an estimated cost and typical treatment time for someone with [my age/issue]?” — You’ll get a ballpark; final estimate after exam.
- “Are retainers included? What if I need an emergency visit?” — Look for inclusive retention and easy emergency access.
- “Do you accept my insurance?” — Confirm billing and any out-of-pocket estimate.

Next step
Tell me your ZIP code and the other details above, and I’ll return a short list (4–6 specific Houston orthodontists/clinics to call) with 1–2 clear reasons to call each, plus their phone number and expected travel area.
